title: Step 2 Phase 5 Rule catalog semantic discovery

mechanics.description: D20_TEST/ABILITY_CHECK
Ability Score and Modifier requires an ability-score-to-modifier mapping and score calculation not represented by the approved Rule mechanics.
On a turn, a creature chooses one listed Action or an Action granted by a feature; the glossary points to twelve named Action records.

conditions: Creature turn
outcomes: One Action is selected from the referenced menu or feature-granted actions.
records.fitRationale: Partial because this glossary rule points to Action-owned turn options and their operation contracts; Rule can preserve the named references, but it does not own their execution semantics.

mechanics.description: The section introduces optional combat Actions, selectable together or individually.

Climb onto Bigger Creature: after DM-required positioning checks, opposed mover Strength (Athletics) or Dexterity (Acrobatics), chosen by mover, versus target Dexterity (Acrobatics); success enters and moves with target space and grants attack Advantage against target. Movement there is Difficult Terrain. Target may spend Action to dislodge via opposed Strength (Athletics) versus mover Strength (Athletics) or Dexterity (Acrobatics), chosen by mover.

Disarm: weapon attack roll contested by target Strength (Athletics) or Dexterity (Acrobatics); success causes no damage/effect and target drops held item. Attacker Disadvantage if item held in two or more hands; target check Advantage if larger, Disadvantage if smaller.

Mark: on melee attack, mark target; until end of attacker next turn, opportunity attacks by attacker against target have Advantage and do not expend Reaction, but cannot occur if reactions are prevented; at most one such opportunity attack per turn.
Overrun: Action or Bonus Action; opposed Strength (Athletics); mover has Advantage if larger, Disadvantage if smaller; success permits one passage through hostile space this turn.
Shove Aside: special Shove attack/check with Disadvantage; successful check moves target 5 feet to a different space within attacker reach.
Tumble: Action or Bonus Action; opposed Dexterity (Acrobatics); success permits one passage through hostile space this turn.

inputs: Mover, hostile creature, larger creature, attacker, defender, marked target, held object
Action or Bonus Action for Overrun/Tumble; Action for Climb and dislodging
conditions: Action Options are optional rules selected by the DM individually or as a group.
Overrun/Tumble require attempting to pass through a hostile creature space.
Climb requires positioning/jumping and a larger target; checks are DM-adjudicated.
outcomes: Procedures grant traversal, shared-space entry, attack modifier, disarm, mark, lateral displacement, or dislodging according to the distinct option.
exceptions: Overrun has size-based advantage/disadvantage.
Climb movement within the larger creature space treats it as Difficult Terrain; attack advantage applies against the host.
Shove Aside moves sideways within reach, not away.
records.fitRationale: Partial because these optional combat procedures are Action-owned and include spatial adjudication, opposed checks, and several distinct outcomes not encoded by this Rule record; exact Action and Skill dependencies remain external.

mechanics.description: Adamantine melee weapons and ammunition are unusually effective at breaking objects: a hit against an object is a critical hit. Adamantine weapon/ammunition versions cost 500 gp above the normal item cost.

conditions: Weapon or ammunition is made of or coated with adamantine; attack hits an object.
outcomes: Hit against an object is critical; item price increases by 500 gp.
records.fitRationale: Partial because the critical-hit-on-object interaction is represented conceptually, while weapon/material identity, item price adjustment, object targeting, and object damage belong to Equipment and object-state contracts.

mechanics.description: D20_TEST/TEST_MODIFIER
Adventure is defined as a series of Encounters; play produces a story.

Alien technology use is learned through repeated Intelligence checks. Simple items require two successes; complex items require four. Four or more failures before a Long Rest may break the item. Prior use or observation grants Advantage. A check-total table assigns failure/success and next-check modifiers; low results can waste a charge/use.

conditions: Repeated Intelligence checks; count successes and failures; Long Rest bounds failure count.
outcomes: Success thresholds reveal operation; failures may waste a use or break item; table modifies next-check Advantage/Disadvantage.
exceptions: Breakage is expressed as DM consideration (?consider making?), not mandatory.
records.fitRationale: Partial because the repeated Intelligence-check learning procedure and its failure/use table are observed, but item complexity, charge consumption, breakage state, and check-result progression require Item/Equipment state and linked check-result procedures.

mechanics.description: Alignment is descriptive characterization: morality axis (good/evil/neutral) and order axis (lawful/chaotic/neutral) yield nine combinations. No independent procedure is stated.
Ally is a relational role: party membership, friendship, combat side, or a rule/DM designation qualifies a creature as an ally.
At level 20, DM may grant one of two repeatable alternatives to an Epic Boon: Ability Score Improvement (+2 one score or +1 two scores, score cap 30) or a player-chosen feat subject to DM approval.

conditions: Reward given instead of Epic Boon; each option may be awarded more than once.
outcomes: Ability score increase or new feat; Ability Score Improvement can exceed 20 to maximum 30.
dependencies: Character Building: ability scores, feats, advancement/reward
records.fitRationale: Partial because this optional reward delegates a choice between ability-score advancement and a feat; level progression, score limits, feat identity, and DM approval belong to Character Building.

mechanics.description: Area of Effect references six geometric shapes. Shape rules determine origin placement. A location is excluded if every straight line from origin is blocked; total cover blocks a line. An unseen origin placed beyond an intervening obstruction appears on the near side of that obstruction.

inputs: Area shape, origin, obstruction, target location, creator perception
conditions: All straight lines to a location are blocked; obstruction provides Total Cover.
outcomes: Location excluded from area; unseen origin can be constrained to near side.
records.fitRationale: Partial because the record references six separately defined shapes and adds cover-based affected-space exclusion and origin placement; the schema has only limited geometry and cannot link all shape procedures as one area-resolution model.

mechanics.description: Armor Class requires a base AC calculation and choice among competing calculations; the Rule contract only references AC as an attack target.

Wearing Light, Medium, or Heavy armor without its training imposes Disadvantage on Strength- or Dexterity-involving D20 Tests and prevents spellcasting. Using a shield without training removes its AC bonus.

conditions: Creature lacks training for worn armor or used shield.
outcomes: Specified D20 Tests have Disadvantage; spellcasting prohibited; shield AC bonus not gained.
records.fitRationale: Partial because its D20 disadvantage is typed-compatible, but armor/shield training state, AC bonus removal, and spellcasting prohibition depend on Equipment, Character proficiency, and Spellcasting.

mechanics.description: D20_TEST/ATTACK_ROLL
A Monster has a starting attitude toward a Player Character selected from Friendly, Hostile, or Indifferent.
Some magic items require attunement before their magical properties can be used; a creature may be attuned to no more than three magic items simultaneously.

conditions: Item requires attunement.
outcomes: Attunement enables use of magical properties, capped at three items.
records.fitRationale: Partial because the numeric three-item limit is explicit, but item identity, attunement lifecycle, and a creature's changing attuned-item set are Equipment/character-state responsibilities.

mechanics.description: Automatic Success requires a DC-versus-ability-score formula, a proficiency-dependent branch, and explicit contest/save/attack exclusions not represented by the approved Rule contract.
Bonus Action is available on the same turn as an Action; at most one per turn, and only when a rule explicitly grants one.

conditions: A rule explicitly grants a Bonus Action.
outcomes: One Bonus Action maximum during that turn.

mechanics.description: Objects can be attacked or affected by spells; DM may allow automatic break of an exceedingly fragile object with Attack or Utilize.
Material-indexed suggested Object AC values: 11 cloth/paper/rope; 13 crystal/glass/ice; 15 wood; 17 stone; 19 iron/steel; 21 mithral; 23 adamantite.
Object destroyed at 0 HP; size/fragility-indexed HP table through Large; larger objects tracked in sections and DM decides if section destruction collapses whole.
Objects immune to Poison and Psychic; DM may change damage-type efficacy; examples describe Bludgeoning/Fabric vs Fire.
Large objects may have Damage Threshold.
Objects lack ability scores unless assigned; no-score objects cannot check and fail all saves.

records.fitRationale: Partial fit: Rule defines material-indexed object AC, size/fragility HP, segmented large objects, thresholds, damage immunities, and zero-ability outcomes; current Rule components do not encode object-durability profiles.

mechanics.description: Bright Light is defined as normal illumination.
Burrow Speed permits movement through sand, earth, mud, or ice; solid rock is excluded absent a trait granting that capability.

conditions: Creature uses Burrow Speed in a listed material.
outcomes: Movement permitted; solid rock remains prohibited unless a trait allows it.
exceptions: Solid-rock exception is trait-dependent.
records.fitRationale: Partial fit: The contract has a generic movement family but does not express substrate permissions or the solid-rock exception.

mechanics.description: Campaign is defined as a series of Adventures.
Cantrip is a level 0 spell cast without a spell slot.

outcomes: Level 0 casting uses no spell slot.
records.fitRationale: Partial because the entry defines a Spell level and spell-slot exception whose complete identity and casting/resource behavior belong to Spell and Character spellcasting contracts.

mechanics.description: Carrying capacity and drag/lift/push maximums depend on creature size and Strength score. Carrying weight above carry capacity limits Speed to no more than 5 feet. A size-indexed table gives Strength multipliers for carry and drag/lift/push.

conditions: Weight being dragged/lifted/pushed exceeds maximum carry weight.
outcomes: Speed capped at 5 feet; size/Strength-derived carry and manipulation limits.
dependencies: Character/creature Strength and size; encumbrance, equipment weight, Speed

mechanics.description: Challenge Rating summarizes threat to a group of four Player Characters and is compared with character level as a planning heuristic; circumstances and group size can alter actual threat. DMG gives encounter-planning guidance.

conditions: Use during encounter planning.
outcomes: Qualitative threat estimate; not deterministic resolution.
dependencies: Creature stat block and encounter planning
records.fitRationale: Partial because CR is a threat-planning heuristic tied to Monster statistics, party size, and encounter context; the Rule schema does not own creature stat blocks or encounter composition.

mechanics.description: Character sheet is a paper or digital record used to track character information; no game procedure is specified.

Optional cleaving rule: if a melee attack reduces an undamaged creature to 0 HP, excess damage may carry to another creature in reach if the same attack roll hits; repeat only while each undamaged target is reduced to 0 HP. DM may use it to speed horde combat.

records.fitRationale: Partial fit: Rule defines conditional carry-through of excess damage only after a qualifying melee hit/reduction and repeated target checks; approved damage structures do not model chained target resolution.

mechanics.description: Climb Speed may replace ordinary Speed for vertical traversal without the usual extra climbing movement cost.

Climbing costs one extra foot per foot moved, or two extra feet in Difficult Terrain; using Climb Speed avoids the surcharge. Slippery surfaces or few handholds may, at DM option, require DC 15 Strength (Athletics).

records.fitRationale: Partial fit: The contract does not fully express climb cost by terrain, Climb Speed override, and optional surface/handhold check.

mechanics.description: Conditions are temporary states whose definitions supply effects and whose ending procedures come from rules; condition effects do not stack with themselves, except Exhaustion.
Lists the XPHB condition entities as references.

records.fitRationale: Partial because the entry gives general non-stacking semantics and a catalog of Condition identities; individual effects and ending procedures belong to Condition records, while the general stacking rule is not a Rule mechanic subtype.

mechanics.description: Cone area widens linearly from its origin: width at a point equals distance from origin; creating effect sets maximum length.
Cone origin is excluded unless creator chooses inclusion.
Cover gives Half Cover +2 AC and Dexterity saves; Three-Quarters Cover +5 to both; Total Cover bars direct targeting. If multiple degrees apply, use only the most protective.

records.fitRationale: Partial because numeric AC/save bonuses and the Total Cover targeting restriction are source-defined, but applying them requires encounter geometry and attack/save targeting state not owned by the static Rule record.

mechanics.description: Spelljamming ship crash: ship moves into target space and rolls d20 + spelljammer proficiency against target AC; hit crashes, miss makes target move out. DM may declare unavoidable crash without roll.

Crash deals size-indexed bludgeoning damage to ship and struck creature/object when damage is plausible; a target without HP means only ship takes damage. Ship stops on Gargantuan or immovable target; otherwise may continue and struck target moves to nearest unoccupied space outside path.
After crash, overlapping gravity-plane suppression may cause creatures aboard to fall; falling damage refers to PHB.
Damage table: Large 4d10, Huge 8d10, Gargantuan 16d10.

records.fitRationale: Partial because ship movement, crash attack resolution, size-based damage, collision continuation, gravity-plane effects, and falling are a linked Vehicle/Encounter procedure; the current Rule mechanics cannot model ship/object spatial state.

mechanics.description: Crawling costs one extra foot per foot, or two extra feet in Difficult Terrain.
Creature is the inclusive game category for any being, including a Player Character.
Creature type is a tag identifying creature category; lists fourteen types, while explicitly stating types have no rules themselves and other rules may use them.
Standard spelljammer complement includes captain, spelljammer, and weapon-operating crew; additional crew/passengers affect ship-air degradation rate.
Spellcaster helmsman typically charges at least 50 gp per operating day.

records.fitRationale: Partial because crew roles and their effect on ship-air depletion are stated, but vessel occupancy, crew assignment, passenger counts, and paid service are Vehicle and campaign-state data.

mechanics.description: D20_TEST/ATTACK_ROLL
DAMAGE_HEALTH_STATE/DAMAGE
Cube area has origin anywhere on a face; effect sets side length.
Origin excluded unless creator chooses otherwise.
Curses are defined by the effect imposing them; Remove Curse, Greater Restoration, or other magic explicitly ending curses can remove them.

records.fitRationale: Partial because the source delegates curse effects and termination to the imposing effect and named magic; the Rule record can preserve that boundary but cannot define each curse or Spell outcome.

mechanics.description: Optional ability-score generation allocates 27 points across six scores.
Table maps scores 8?15 to point costs 0,1,2,3,4,5,7,9; scores cannot be below 8 or above 15 before racial increases.
Examples illustrate possible distributions; an internal link points to a point-buy calculator.

records.fitRationale: Partial because the point-buy budget and score-cost table are explicit, but applying the optional generation method and racial increases belongs to Character Building; examples and calculator links are not additional mechanics.

mechanics.description: Optional origin rules permit reallocating racial ability increases, languages, and listed proficiencies within constraints; ability-score increases cannot stack on one score and scores cannot exceed 20.
Language trait selections may be replaced from a named language list, subject to DM additions/removals.
Proficiencies can be exchanged under a table mapping Skill, armor, weapon, and tool categories.
Custom Lineage defines a selectable Humanoid/size/speed/ability/feat/trait/language package; personality guidance is player-controlled.

records.fitRationale: Partial because this optional package changes ancestry ability, language, and proficiency selections under constraints; those selectable identities and replacement effects belong to Character Building, Language, and Skill.

mechanics.description: Cylinder area origin is at center of circular top or bottom; effect specifies base radius and height.
Cylinder origin is included.
D20_TEST/TEST
Damage reduces Hit Points of a creature or object.
Damage roll is a die roll adjusted by applicable modifiers that deals damage to a target.
Damage threshold grants immunity to an instance of damage below threshold; a single attack/effect meeting or exceeding threshold deals the entire instance.
Lists thirteen damage types and examples; types have no rules themselves but Resistance and other mechanics can rely on them. Table examples guide DM assignment to new effects.
An area of Darkness is Heavily Obscured.
Dead creature has 0 HP and cannot regain HP until revived by magic; spirit may refuse revival and must be called back.
Revival sets current HP per effect; ongoing conditions, magical contagions, and curses return if their durations continue; Exhaustion returns one level lower; attunement ends.

records.fitRationale: Partial because revival consequences depend on the chosen magic effect, ongoing effect durations, Disease/Condition state, and attunement; the Rule schema cannot coordinate those external lifecycles.

mechanics.description: D20_TEST/DEATH_SAVING_THROW
The Rule schema has no bounded Player Character actor applicability and no canonical Player Character Rule target is available.
Optional grid rule replaces PHB diagonal counting for more geometrically realistic range/movement.
Diagonal squares count alternately 5 feet then 10 feet; pattern continues across intervening straight movement.
Example totals demonstrate the alternating rule.

records.fitRationale: Partial because alternating 5/10-foot diagonal distance is a discrete grid-distance procedure absent from the movement contract; the examples confirm the counting rule but are not separate mechanics.

mechanics.description: MOVEMENT_SPATIAL/DIFFICULT_TERRAIN
Difficulty Class is a general target-number definition spanning checks and saves; no standalone DC-definition component exists.
Dim Light area is Lightly Obscured.
D20_TEST/TEST_MODIFIER
Stronghold requires acquired land; kingdom land may need charter, land grant, deed, inheritance, or other acquisition. Costs vary by estate.
After securing estate, construction requires materials and labor; table defines nine structure costs and build times.
Downtime supervision determines base construction time; work continues while absent but each absence day adds three construction days.
Magic-item search requires at least one workweek and 100 gp; more time/cost may improve item quality.

Charisma (Persuasion) determines seller/item tier; +1 per extra workweek and each extra 100 gp, capped +10. Campaign magic level may add +/-10 and low-magic campaigns may double prices. DM chooses stock and final price.
Specific desired-item availability has rarity thresholds of 10/15/20/25/30 for common through legendary.
Check-total table selects magic-item table and roll count; lower-tier tables are allowed.
Rarity-based asking-price dice; consumables are half price.
Optional complication table for magic-item purchase; DM may instead invent complication.
Carousing is a downtime option; wealthy lifestyle expenditure applies.
At end of selected downtime period, roll d100 plus character level; DM or table determines outcome.
Outcome bands can impose jail/fine, robbery, hostile relationship, romance, or gambling income and lifestyle-cost recovery.

One workweek and expense by social class; upper-class access requires nobility access or sufficient contacts judged by DM. Noble background permits mingling; disguise kit and Deception may support other entry.
After a workweek, Charisma (Persuasion) check yields contacts by check-total bands: hostile, none, one, two, or three allied contacts.
Contacts have bounded aid/hindrance behavior and one-use help/hinder; another carouse is needed to restore goodwill.
Contact social class depends on where character caroused; unspecified allied contacts cap at 1 + Charisma modifier, minimum 1; named contacts do not count.
Each workweek has 10% complication chance; class-specific tables provide examples.
Nonmagical crafting requires appropriate tool proficiency and may require special materials or location.
Each downtime day completes up to 5 gp market value and consumes raw materials worth half value; higher-value work accrues in 5 gp increments.
Collaborators each contribute 5 gp/day if proficient and co-located.
Crafting permits modest lifestyle at no daily cost or comfortable lifestyle at half cost.
DOWNTIME_PROCEDURE/ACTIVITY

The approved Rule schema cannot model the precise optionality, prerequisites, rarity tables, cost/work formula, spell-slot/material expenditure, cooperative contributions, campaign choices, or lifestyle exception without loss.
The approved downtime component has no formula model or rarity/cost table.
Nonmagical crafting uses materials worth half sale cost; time is cost/50 gp in workweeks. Multiple items up to 50 gp/workweek; safe storage needed for longer work.
Collaborative crafting divides required time by worker count, subject to DM capacity judgment.
All workers need relevant proficiency and equipment; table gives tool-to-item examples.
Craft result is item; crafted item can be sold at listed price.
Magic-item crafting requires formula, rare material/adventure, rarity/CR association, cost/time table, suitable tool or Arcana proficiency; consumables halve listed cost and time.
Each five workweeks of magic crafting has 10% complication chance; table examples are not deterministic procedures.
Healing potion crafting has separate herbalism proficiency, time, and cost schedule.
Crime preparation consumes one week and at least 25 gp.
Player chooses DC 10/15/20/25; three checks are Dexterity (Stealth), Dexterity with thieves? tools, and one of Intelligence (Investigation), Wisdom (Perception), or Charisma (Deception).
Payout depends on DC; 0 successes means caught, fine equal to intended profit and one jail week per 25 gp; 1 success escapes but fails; 2 earns half; 3 earns full.
Loot table maps DC to payout.
Complication is triggered on one success, or two if rival involved in crime/law enforcement; examples table.
Combined downtime days on minor tasks/socializing equal current organizational Renown ? 10 increase Renown by 1.
Gambling takes a workweek and stake at least 10 gp; source leaves upper stake limit to DM.
Three checks: Wisdom (Insight), Charisma (Deception), Charisma (Intimidation); suitable gaming-set proficiency can replace relevant skill. Each check gets independent random DC 5 + 2d10.
Success count determines loss/debt, half loss, stake plus half gain, or double stake.
Each gambling workweek has 10% complication chance; table supplies examples.
After at least 10 days performing temple rites, gain Inspiration each day for the next 2d6 days.
Pit fighting consumes one workweek.

Three checks with independently randomized DCs (5+2d10): Strength (Athletics), Dexterity (Acrobatics), and Constitution with bonus equal to largest Hit Die roll without spending die; one skill check may be replaced by weapon attack roll. Success count determines 0/50/100/200 gp.
Each workweek has 10% complication chance; examples include rivalry and injury.
Work supports modest lifestyle without daily expense while profession continues.
Organization-provided employment raises support to comfortable lifestyle.
Performance proficiency used during downtime raises support to wealthy lifestyle.
Downtime can recover from injury, disease, or poison.
After three recuperation days, DC 15 Constitution save; on success choose one of listed outcomes.
Can end one effect preventing HP recovery.
For 24 hours, gain Advantage on saves against one current Disease or Poison.
One week of relaxation; at least modest lifestyle required.

While relaxing, Advantage on saves to recover from long-acting diseases/poisons. At week end, end one effect preventing HP recovery or restore one reduced ability score. Cannot use benefit for ongoing spell/magical effect.
Complication is DM-introduced if desired; no fixed procedure.
Religious service requires access/attendance at aligned temple; one workweek, no gold cost.
Choose Intelligence (Religion) or Charisma (Persuasion); check total awards 0/1/2 favors.
Favor may grant future temple support or halve cleric spellcasting cost; DM may determine divine intervention form.
Unused favors capped at 1 + Charisma modifier, minimum 1.
10% complication chance per service workweek; table examples.
Research needs library or sage access, one workweek, and 50 gp baseline.
Character chooses topic; after week, Intelligence check gains +1 per extra 50 gp capped +6; well-stocked library/sages grant Advantage. Outcome table yields 0?3 true statements by total.
DM determines content of information; examples are illustrative.
10% complications chance each workweek; examples include false information but do not define a mandatory outcome.
DM determines information availability, days, restrictions, and optional checks; when conditions are met, available information is learned.
Research costs 1 gp per day in addition to normal lifestyle.
Roll d100 plus days spent, capped at 30, to resolve business maintenance/profit.
Unpaid required costs cause failure and -10 on subsequent table rolls for each unpaid debt.
Result bands determine maintenance cost fraction, whether costs are covered, and possible profits.
Scroll crafting requires time/cost by spell level, Arcana proficiency, required material components, and spell prepared or known; cantrip scroll functions as if caster level 1.
Table defines duration and cost from cantrip through level 9.
10% complication chance per workweek; examples include random replacement spell.
Finding buyer for one selected magic item takes one workweek and 25 gp.
Persuasion check sets offer tier; seller may decline and retry later, forfeiting prior workweek. Tables establish rarity base price and 50/100/150% offer bands.
10% complication chance each workweek; table examples.
Only common through very rare items; requires suitable market and buyer search, legendary/artifacts need adventure.
DC 20 Investigation finds buyer: failure takes 10 days; success time is rarity-dependent; another character can grant Advantage.
Multiple-item checks/searches are simultaneous and results are not aggregated.
Per item, percentile roll adjusted by rarity plus Persuasion total determines offer; table includes legitimate and shady buyers.
DM determines buyer identity/legal consequence.
Rumor duration depends on settlement size; town/city effort must be continuous or rumor fades.

Cost 1 gp/day; after required period DC 15 Charisma (Deception or Persuasion); success shifts general community attitude one step toward chosen friendly/hostile direction, failure prevents further propagation attempts.
Community shift does not compel every individual; personal experience can preserve individual attitude.
Optional training can teach new language or tool set; DM may allow more training options.
Instructor required; DM determines duration and optional checks.
Source default is 250 days at 1 gp/day; completion grants language or tool proficiency.
Training can teach language or tool proficiency if instructor/time available.
Typically ten workweeks reduced by Intelligence modifier (penalty does not increase duration); cost 25 gp/workweek.
Each ten workweeks has 10% complication chance; examples are teacher events.
Variant delays new-level class features until required downtime training after earning enough XP.
Training days/cost depend on attained level; table groups levels 2?4/5?10/11?16/17?20 at 10/20/30/40 days and 20/40/60/80 gp.
One workweek job uses one selected ability check: Strength (Athletics), Dexterity (Acrobatics), Intelligence with tools, Charisma (Performance), or Charisma with instrument.
Check total determines lifestyle/pay band from poor to comfortable +25 gp.
Each workweek has 10% complication chance; examples can reduce wages, prevent pay, or impose future check Disadvantage for six workweeks.
Spend rank-scaled workweeks and funds to explore territory; one Wisdom (Survival) check is modified by added investment and named staff, capped at +10.
Check-total bands select territorial discoveries, cost changes, durations, allies/creatures, and optional complications.

inputs: Territory, rank, weeks, gp, staff, Survival total.
conditions: Minimum time and investment; additional spend/time increases check bonus.
outcomes: Bands generate hazards or resources and temporary monthly-cost effects.
exceptions: Complications are optional; some benefits last until DM resolves threat.
dependencies: AI franchise rank/staff, ally/monster identities and cost system.

mechanics.description: Two sequentially distinct checks establish vision and team acceptance, each with DC 13 + rank and role/position modifiers.
Extra work and money grant capped modifiers; number of successes selects monthly cost change/duration and complication chance.

inputs: Rank; two checks and checkers; time/gp; staff roles; position.
conditions: At least two weeks and rank-based cost; separate check ability/skill choices.
outcomes: 0?2 successes set cost adjustment and duration.
exceptions: DM selects checks and may add complications on success.

mechanics.description: Modify an existing headquarters feature with DM approval; procedure requires lead and two additional checks plus time, staff, and funds.
Three-check outcome sets cost overrun, future advantage, drawback, and complications.

inputs: HQ feature; rank; staff; weeks/gp; participants and checks.
conditions: Majordomo, staffing and time prerequisites; DM may require adventure/side trek.
outcomes: Outcome depends on count of successful checks.
exceptions: DM may substitute checks; feature choice/frequency constrained by DM.
dependencies: AI HQ/features, role and rank tables.

mechanics.description: Three separate ability checks execute an approved marketing plan with separately rolled DCs.
Rank-scaled time/cost, bounded added spending and staff modifiers affect checks; aggregate success alters monthly costs.

inputs: Plan; three checks; rank; time/gp; staff.
conditions: DM approves plan/check selection; min time/cost; +1 bonus spending capped per check.
outcomes: Success count 0?3 maps to cost reductions/durations.
exceptions: DM may add complication.
dependencies: AI franchise accounting and staff roles.

mechanics.description: Philanthropic project targets a nearby cause and requires rank-scaled work and funds plus a DM-selected ability check.
Check-total bands determine harm/no improvement/praise or stronger effects, payments, and temporary cost reduction.

conditions: Cause nearby; min time/cost.
outcomes: Total bands set social/cause outcome, honorarium, or temporary cost effect.
exceptions: DM chooses check and whether to add complications.

mechanics.description: At month end, d100 plus player-allocated staff/character days selects a franchise monthly-cost modifier.
Effects from activities aggregate; cost reductions can eliminate payment or create profit; failure to pay risks franchise failure.

inputs: Month; d100; days allocated; rank/HQ and other activity effects.
conditions: Runs monthly even unstaffed; adventure days excluded.
outcomes: Bands alter monthly cost; aggregate reduction can become profit.
exceptions: DM may waive roll; failures/complications use franchise rules.
dependencies: AI Franchise Costs, ranks and HQ.

mechanics.description: Schmoozing targets a named NPC or group representative; time/cost tier and Charisma (Persuasion) check determine relationship result.
Bands grant relationship/favor or disrepute and can alter later check advantage; duration/content are DM-defined.

inputs: NPC/group; social tier; rank; week/gp; Persuasion; background/role.
conditions: Target tier sets cost; role/background can modify check.
outcomes: Check bands: disrepute, confidante, friend, favor.
exceptions: DM determines relationship duration, favor and complications.

mechanics.description: Scrutineering requires DM-set access/resources and uses time, rank-scaled spending and a modified Intelligence check.
Check-total bands give up to three DM-selected lore facts; complication is a separate optional table.

inputs: Topic/access; rank; weeks/gp; Intelligence check and Skill; staff.
conditions: Access/resources established first; additional spending/role add capped bonus.
outcomes: Outcome gives zero to three facts.
exceptions: DM selects lore and complication.

mechanics.description: DM-approved scheme uses three separately DC-set ability checks selected to fit plan and narrative.
Success total determines arrest/fine or profits/benefits; optional ongoing scheme costs a recurring 10-percent cut.

inputs: Scheme; three checks; rank; weeks/gp; background; revenue.
conditions: DM approves scheme/checks; at least two weeks and base cost.
outcomes: 0?3 successes yield fine or rank-scaled profit/benefits.
exceptions: Optional ongoing payment and complication; DM determines check.
dependencies: AI franchise rank, economy, legal setting.

mechanics.description: At least two participants create reciprocal partner-linked stories and make individual Wisdom (Insight) checks.
Check bands grant partner-relative penalties/bonuses or a memory; memory can grant one 10-minute Enhance Ability-like benefit.

inputs: Participants, selected partners, bonds/ideals, check, time and staff role.
conditions: May be required by DM; minimum two participants/week; alternate checks are DM-approved.
outcomes: Check bands set partner-linked check effects or replaceable memory.
exceptions: DM judges story quality and complications.
dependencies: Character bonds/ideals, franchise roles, spell effect.

mechanics.description: Downtime units vary by activity; workdays may be nonconsecutive, require daily minimum hours, and fit within an elapsed-time ceiling.
Rival NPC advances a plan per workweek; excess elapsed time can add complications or double activity costs.

mechanics.description: Feywild departure: Wisdom save with Fey/trait exceptions; failure erases visit memory; curse-ending magic restores memory; separate time-warp choice/table and Wish removal.

Outer-plane alignment incompatibility can cause end-of-Long-Rest Constitution save and Exhaustion; lawful/chaotic difference excluded.
Good-aligned Mount Celestia visitor receives Bless while present and Lesser Restoration benefit after Long Rest.
Bytopia visitor save may change alignment; 1d4-day plane-exit timing determines permanence/reversion; Dispel Evil and Good restores.
Elysium Long Rest failures can compel another rest; three failures make voluntary departure cease; Dispel Evil and Good ends it.
Beastlands grants Advantage on listed Animal Handling, Perception, and Survival checks.
Slaying native Beast triggers Charisma save or Polymorph-like beast transformation; repeat at Long Rest; three failures restrict cure to Remove Curse or similar.
Leaving Arborea after tracked days triggers increasing-DC Charisma save; failure imposes check Disadvantage with Long Rest retries/magic cure.
On Ysgard, non-Construct/non-Undead creature killed by attack/spell returns at next dawn with HP restored and pre-death Conditions/afflictions removed.
Limbo Action checks manipulate visible objects within 30 feet, transform an eligible unattended nonmagical object, or stabilize a radius for 24 hours; size/radius determines DC and success result.
Pandemonium hourly Wisdom save grants Exhaustion on failure; at level six creature instead gains random indefinite Madness; Long Rest cannot remove Exhaustion while exposed.

Acheron grants temporary HP equal to half maximum when creature reduces hostile creature to zero HP.
Mechanus replaces rolled attack/spell damage with average damage.
